svg.title: ExplainSQL on a slow query: the verdict, the slowest node, why the planner uses no index, the suggested index measured in a rolled-back transaction, and the locks the statement takes
svg.desc: Recorded from a real run of explainsql 0.2.0 against PostgreSQL 16.15.

g.text: The query: a customer's order summary
SELECT c.name, count(*) AS orders, sum(o.amount) AS total
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
Enter EXPLAIN ANALYZE on PostgreSQL 16.15, rolled back
13.4 ms. 99% of it in Seq Scan on orders o, which reads 200,000 rows to keep 10.

Why does Seq Scan on orders o not use an index?
No index can serve the condition of Seq Scan on orders o: even with sequential scans off, the planner
no index on orders starts with customer_id
Create an index that serves the condition: see the advice.

L the locks the statement takes, and what would wait for them
13.4 ms. 99% of it in Seq Scan on orders o, which reads 200,000 rows to keep 10.
3 locks: AccessShareLock on the table, 2 indexes (the plan uses none)
2 locks: AccessShareLock on the table, 1 index
The planner locks every index of the tables it plans, used or not: orders_created_at_idx is
not used by this plan and not scanned since the statistics began.
→ An index nothing uses adds a lock to every run of every statement on its table, and work to
every write: drop it, after checking the statistics of every server that runs queries (replicas
These commands would wait for the statement's locks, and while they wait, every later run of the
- ALTER TABLE (most forms), DROP, TRUNCATE, REINDEX, CLUSTER, VACUUM FULL, LOCK TABLE on orders
- REINDEX, DROP INDEX or ALTER INDEX of any of the 3 indexes it locks, 2 of which the plan does
not use: the planner locks every index of a table it plans
→ In schema changes, SET lock_timeout = '2s' (or so) makes a command that has to wait give up
instead of holding up every query on the table; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and REINDEX CONCURRENTLY
